input.quote: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 grants unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems — squarely in walk-away territory under the AUDIT rule (no frequency limit, no notice, direct system access). Sections 22.2 and 22.3 already provide the protective cost allocation (Vendor bears costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent) and confidentiality of findings, so the minimal fix is to add frequency, notice, business-hours and off-site/independent-auditor limits to 22.1 and delete the remote-access language, reaching the preferred position.

proposal.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, off-site by an independent auditor, with no access to Customer systems.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We limited audits to once per twelve months on thirty days' written notice, during business hours and conducted off-site by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and removed remote access to our systems, consistent with our playbook position and Section 22.2. If helpful, we can accept fifteen days' notice.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's usage of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours and without unreasonable disruption. The audit shall be conducted off-site wherever practicable by an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, and shall be limited to records reasonably necessary to verify usage. Vendor and its auditor have no right to access Customer's systems, whether remotely or on-site.
